newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania president steps in to calm coalition row.
newsitem.headline: Romania president steps in to calm coalition row.

text.p: Romania's President Emil Constantinescu on Thursday stepped in to defuse a row among ruling centrist coalition partners who took office after ousting ex-communists in elections last year.
Constantinescu summoned Christian Democrats and their junior coalition partners, Social Democrats, Liberal and ethnic Hungarian minority leaders, for talks at his Cotroceni palace.
The talks were an attempt to smoothe frictions within the coalition pitting Prime Minister Petre Roman's Democrats against the senior partners the National Peasant Party (PNTCD).
"The coalition must continue to work because it has a vital role in Romania's future," said a PNTCD statement issued after the Cotroceni palace talks.

The row erupted earlier this week when a government official issued a report on alleged illegal house purchases in the post-communist era involving Roman and several other key Democratic Party figures.

Roman's Democrats hold the foreign affairs, defence and transport portfolios in the coalition government, headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, whose PNTCD also leads the centrist alliance which dominates parliament.
Roman has threatened to quit the alliance unless his Democrats were cleared of the accusations in the report, which he dismissed as "calumnies".

"If we are corrupt we should not be part of this government," Roman, head of the upper Senate house, effectively the number two job in the state, told a news conference after coalition leaders held talks with Constantinescu.

The centrists, who ended the leftists' seven-year grip on power in the 1996 presidential and parliamentary polls, have vowed tough reforms, in exchange for resumed credits from international lenders, to put the economy on a market footing.
Constantinescu left for Ukraine later on Thursday for talks with the Ukrainian and Moldovan presidents to boost ties with the two former Soviet republics.
